title: Analyzing Social Stratification Models
text:
Social stratification refers to a system by which a society ranks categories of people into a hierarchy. Key sociological perspectives, such as those developed by Karl Marx and Max Weber, analyze this structure using different metrics—capital (Marx focusing on economic means), status (Weber's honor/prestige), and power. These frameworks demonstrate that social standing is rarely determined solely by individual effort but rather by inherited and systemic advantages.

The maintenance of these hierarchical structures is often achieved through cultural mechanisms, including the accumulation and valuation of specific knowledge or skills, termed cultural capital. Institutional policies and ingrained norms further reinforce inequality, suggesting that seemingly meritocratic systems can perpetuate cycles of disadvantage across generations.
